subject: Scaling pathway amendment negotiation: temporary rate lock and commit ramp
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@tesserasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal window + scaling pathway — draft amendment attached

Elena —

Hope your week is going well. Tessera's renewal is up in January and I wanted to align early given your expected volume growth. From our last call you described a phased ramp: +2x tokens Q1 -> Q2 and an additional +50% in Q3 if the new search feature performs.

To keep pricing predictable while you scale, I attached a short amendment draft that includes: a 6-month temporary rate lock for your current committed tiers, a staged commit ramp (quarterly checkpoints), and a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration overhead. The draft also includes a short true-up window (30 days) to accelerate visibility during the ramp.

Key ask: can you share a target monthly token range for Jan–Jun so we can model the commit ladder and the credit sizing? If agreeable, I can circulate a v2 that maps concrete numbers and a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Attachment: tesserasys-amendment-v1.pdf (summary + proposed terms)

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@tesserasys.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessera Procurement <procurement@tesserasys.com>, Matthew Cho <matt.cho@tesserasys.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window + scaling pathway — draft amendment attached

Dylan —

Thanks for the draft and for getting ahead of this. A few clarifying notes from our side after internal ops and procurement reviewed:

- We like the idea of a short-term rate lock while we ramp, but procurement prefers a 3-month ramp check-in cadence to avoid committing too far out.
- The true-up window of 30 days works operationally, but can you show a model where overages are billed monthly rather than at renewal? We need predictable cash flows.
- For the onboarding credit: we need the dollar math. Can you convert the proposed percentage into an explicit credit amount tied to the Q1 expected delta?

High-level numbers: our preliminary run-rate target is ~120M tokens/month in Jan, 240M in Apr, 360M in Jul if the feature hits. We'll share the workbook with a finalized forecast early next week.

Can you circulate a v2 with: (A) a 3-month checkpoint cadence, (B) monthly overage billing model, and (C) the credit expressed as a $ number and applied pro rata across the first two billing periods? Also include an SLA credit clause for downtime > 99.5% during the expansion window — procurement will require it in any amendment.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Product Operations, Tessera Systems
elena.soto@tesserasys.com

Subject: Fwd: Renewal window + scaling pathway — Tessera feedback (procurement asks)

Team — forwarding Tessera's asks below. Highlights: they want a 3-month checkpoint cadence (not 6), monthly overage billing, explicit $ credit amount, and an SLA credit clause during the expansion window. Their preliminary forecast attached separately.

Proposed internal approach (quick):
- Offer a 3-month checkpoint cadence but keep a staged commit ladder to secure volume economics.
- Provide a one-time committed credit of $50,000 (instead of a percentage) applied pro rata across months 1–2 of the ramp.
- Provide a 6-month temporary rate lock on the current committed per-token price, subject to the checkpoint outcomes; after 6 months, normal pricing applies unless checkpoint upgrades are executed.
- Agree to monthly overage billing with a capped surge rate at 1.25x the committed rate above a burst threshold.
- Include an SLA credit clause limited to service unavailability > 99.5% and capped per quarter.

I've attached a revised amendment (v2) that maps the $50k credit and the burst surcharge wording. Please review and flag anything finance/legal will push back on. If we can align, I'll send v2 to Elena and procurement with DocuSign steps.

Attachments: tesserasys-amendment-v2.pdf, tessera-usage-model.xlsx

Thanks —
Dylan

Internal note: aim to keep net economic impact < $75k across the 6mo window
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window + scaling pathway — Tessera feedback (procurement asks)

Dylan —

Thanks for the summary. A few finance constraints and edits we should make before externalizing v2:

1) $50k credit is OK, but finance prefers it be structured as a committed credit (applied against monthly invoices) and only refundable via true-up (not cash).
2) Instead of a flat 1.25x surge rate, propose a two-tier overage schedule: 1.15x for usage up to +30% above committed, then 1.35x beyond +30%. This gives Tessera predictability and protects our margin on unexpected spikes.
3) Require a minimum committed monthly baseline (we suggest 90M tokens/month) during the 6-month lock to avoid excessive downside risk. If they fall below baseline, we reserve the right to re-open pricing at checkpoint.

If you can accept the above, update v2 and I'll sign off from finance. Otherwise, mark items for legal and we can route to them.

-Markus
Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@tesserasys.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessera Procurement <procurement@tesserasys.com>, Matthew Cho <matt.cho@tesserasys.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window + scaling pathway — updated terms

Dylan/Redwood —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement reviewed Markus' two-tier suggestion and the $50k committed credit; they're comfortable with structure as long as: (A) the minimum baseline is 90M tokens/month for the lock period, (B) the credit is applied pro rata across the first two invoices, and (C) the SLA credit language is scaled (example: 5% invoice credit per quarter for availability below 99.5%, max one quarterly credit during the 6-month window).

We accept those constraints in principle. One outstanding ask: can Redwood add an automatic scaling policy in the Console to allow burst capacity to auto-allocate up to 20% beyond committed for short bursts without manual approval? That helps our ops teams avoid throttles while we monitor.

Procurement is ready to execute the amendment pending DocuSign. Can you send a DocuSign-ready package and an updated SOW that calls out the Console auto-scale policy and the checkpoint review dates?

Thanks —
Elena
